title: Discarding writes through a symlink, escaping the workspace
description:
`writeWorkingCopyFile` in index.ts (the discard environment, ~line 573) calls
`writeFile`, which follows a symlink at the destination. The path containment
check added for concern-8 does not cover this: the path is entirely legitimate,
only the destination's type is not.

Trigger: a repository that tracks a symlink — git stores them as ordinary files
— pointing outside the repo, e.g. `link -> ~/.ssh/authorized_keys`, plus an edit
to `link` in the review. Discarding that hunk writes *through* the link, outside
the workspace, with content the patch controls.

The same applies to the jj helper script (src/jj/script.ts): the `cat "$stage/
files/$path" > "$right/$path"` redirect follows a symlink in `$right` the same
way.

`removeWorkingCopyFile` is fine as it stands — `rm` does not follow symlinks.

title: Git-quoted paths are never decoded, so the wrong file is read and written
description:
`stripPathPrefix` in src/patch/parse.ts:68-74 does not unquote. git quotes any
path containing non-ASCII or special characters, writing

    +++ "b/caf\303\251"

rather than `+++ b/café`. The leading `"` makes both `startsWith("a/")` and
`startsWith("b/")` fail, so the prefix is not even stripped: the quotes and the
C-style escapes survive into `patch.path` and are used as a literal filename.
Staging or discarding then reads and writes a file that does not exist under
that name.

A repository containing one non-ASCII filename is enough to trigger this, which
makes it the likeliest of the path findings to be hit by accident rather than by
a hostile patch.

Fix: decode before the prefix strip — detect the surrounding quotes, unescape
`\\`, `\"`, and octal sequences. Related to concern-7 in the doubt session,
which is the other half of path recovery failing quietly instead of loudly.

title: Harden the CI workflow: token permissions, action pinning, jj checksum
description:
Three supply-chain gaps in .github/workflows/ci.yml:

1. No `permissions:` block, so `GITHUB_TOKEN` gets the repository default rather
   than the read access this job needs — and it is handed to a step explicitly
   as `GH_TOKEN` (line 20).
2. Both actions are pinned to floating tags (`actions/checkout@v4`,
   `oven-sh/setup-bun@v2`), so a compromised or retagged release runs with that
   token.
3. The jj release tarball is downloaded and installed with no checksum
   verification, so CI trusts whatever that asset holds at download time.

Fix: `permissions: contents: read` at workflow level, both actions pinned to
commit SHAs, and the jj download verified against the digest published with the
release.

title: Cross-check the parsed path against the path Hunk reports
description:
`findDisagreement` in src/patch/agreement.ts:18-21 compares hunk counts and line
ranges but never the path. `ReviewedFile` carries two: `file.path`, which Hunk
resolved, and `patch.path`, which this extension parsed out of the same text —
and only the second one ever reaches the filesystem, never compared against the
first.

This module exists precisely to refuse when the two parses disagree, so a path
mismatch belongs in it: same class of bug as a hunk-count mismatch, and it costs
one comparison.

It does not replace the containment check added for concern-8 — both sides can
agree on a path that escapes the workspace — but it catches a parser that read
the wrong filename, which containment cannot. Likely to surface the quoted-path
bug (hunk-commit-ys8) as a refusal rather than a wrong write.

title: Check whether diff.relative breaks path resolution
description:
Found while verifying that the concern-8 containment check would not reject
paths when Hunk is launched from a subdirectory. It would not: git and jj both
emit repo-root-relative paths from any directory, and `--relative` omits files
outside the cwd rather than reaching them with `..`.

But that mode raises a separate question. With `diff.relative=true` in git
config, paths become relative to the cwd (`a/foo.ts` for `src/deep/foo.ts` when
run from `src/deep`). `workspace.root` is always the repo root — `detectWorkspace`
walks upward — so `join(workspace.root, path)` would then resolve the wrong
file.

Unverified: whether Hunk passes that config through, or normalises paths before
handing them to an extension. If it does pass through, the failure is loud
(ENOENT into the catch in index.ts) rather than silent, so this is a correctness
question, not a safety one.

Work: confirm what Hunk does with `diff.relative=true`, and fix or document.
